About the Fellowship

The Belgium-funded UN JPO Programme 2026 has opened three posts with a common application deadline of 18 September 2026 at 6:00 p.m. EST (New York time). This is a paid UN professional post (JPO), not a scholarship. The programme is funded by Service public fédéral Affaires étrangères, Commerce extérieur et Coopération au Développement (Belgian FPS Foreign Affairs). Placements are within UN organizations including UNDP, UNICEF, WFP, UNHCR, OCHA, UNRWA, WHO, and approximately 18 partner entities.

The Three Open Positions (August 2026 Call)

  1. JPO in Political Affairs – Support to UN Reform — based in New York, USA, supporting UN development-system reform work.
  2. JPO in Humanitarian Affairs — based in East Jerusalem, engaged in humanitarian coordination in the occupied Palestinian territory context.
  3. JPO in UN System Coordination — based in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire, supporting UN country-team coordination.

Each position has its own vacancy PDF published on the Belgian FPS Foreign Affairs JPO page.

Financial Coverage & Benefits

This is a salaried UN post, not a scholarship. Belgium fully funds the position on behalf of the selected candidate.

  • UN contract at P-2 level with international staff status. Salary paid in US dollars on UN scales (P-2 base salary approximately USD 57,600–78,300 per year, plus post adjustment varying by duty station).
  • Training and mentoring by senior UN staff throughout the assignment, including access to JPO programme learning events.
  • Pension coverage: Belgium pays the pension/ONSS contribution.
  • Contract renewability: initial 1-year contract, renewable up to a maximum of 3 years.
  • Placement within a UN organization that maintains an active cooperation relationship with Belgian international development policy.

Eligibility and Requirements

  • Belgian citizenship: Most posts are reserved for Belgian nationals.
  • Age: No older than 32 on 31 December 2026 (born on or after 1 January 1994).
  • Master's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field.
  • Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience in development cooperation, political affairs, humanitarian action, or the vacancy's subject area.
  • Very good knowledge of English and French.
  • Mobility and willingness to serve at the advertised duty station for up to three years.
  • Note: A limited number of JPO posts are identified in advance for nationals of Belgium's 14 partner countries and are announced separately. Such candidates should monitor the FPS and UNDP JPO pages.

Application dates

MilestoneDate
Application deadline18 September 2026, 6:00 p.m. EST
Selection process durationMinimum approximately 3 months from posting to selection

Application Process

  1. Download the vacancy PDF for the target position from the Belgian FPS Foreign Affairs JPO page.
  2. Apply through the recruiting UN organization's e-recruitment system as directed in each vacancy announcement. Applications go directly to the UN entity, not by email to Belgium.
  3. Prepare the standard UN application package: tailored personal history profile (PHP) or CV, motivation letter, university diplomas, language certificates, and referee contact details.
  4. Submit before 18 September 2026, 6:00 p.m. EST. Late applications are not accepted.
  5. Selection involves CV screening by the UN organization and Belgian government, followed by interviews.

Official Link

  • Belgian FPS Foreign Affairs JPO Programme page: https://diplomatie.belgium.be/fr/travailler-au-spf-affaires-etrangeres/young-professionals/junior-professional-officer
  • UNDP JPO Service Centre Belgium Programme: https://www.undp.org/jposc/belgium
  • UN JPO generic information: https://jpo.desa.un.org

Important Notes

  • This is a fully funded UN professional job with a salary on UN scales, not a study award.
  • Duration of 3 years is the contract ceiling, not a guaranteed term. Appointments start at one year and renew by performance and funding.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 18 September 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
